parts.description: An off-white matte ceramic vessel with a bulbous rounded base, narrow neck, flared rim, and two small side cups with round openings.
parts.reasoning: No product dimensions or measured mass were provided, so the values are estimated from the visible tabletop ceramic form. I assume an overall height of roughly 0.20-0.25 m, a maximum body diameter around 0.11-0.13 m, overall width including the side cups around 0.16-0.18 m, and a ceramic wall thickness of about 4-6 mm. Dense stoneware/ceramic material is typically about 2100-2400 kg/m^3; using 2200 kg/m^3 and a hollow shell with a thickened rim, base, and two side cup features gives an estimated total mass near 0.8-1.1 kg, so 0.9 kg is a practical rigid-body mass. The object is topologically concave: it has an open flared mouth, small cup openings, side protrusions, and undercut transitions between the protrusions and the main body. A single convex hull would incorrectly fill the mouth and side cup cavities, while a low-count convex decomposition may still lose the usable holes; therefore an SDF mesh collider is the best high-fidelity choice in Isaac Sim/PhysX if contacts with the rim, cup openings, or concave surfaces matter. For faster scenes where only the outer silhouette contacts the environment, use convex decomposition with multiple hulls as a performance substitute. The dominant contact material is matte ceramic, so friction is estimated higher than glazed glass but lower than rubber: static friction about 0.55 and dynamic friction about 0.42 against common tabletop materials. Restitution is kept low at 0.22 because real ceramic is hard but brittle and tends to chip, ring, or fracture rather than rebound elastically; a low restitution also prevents unrealistic bouncing for a non-fracturing rigid approximation. Contact offsets are set small for a tabletop-scale object: 0 m rest offset and about 0.0025 m contact offset, large enough for stable PhysX contact generation but small enough not to visibly float the thin rim or cup lips. CCD is enabled because the hard, thin-rimmed geometry can tunnel or miss contacts during fast manipulation or drops. Compliant contacts are disabled because the vessel is modeled as a rigid non-deformable ceramic object; if solver chatter appears with high-speed impacts, a very stiff damped compliant material could be introduced, but the default recommendation is rigid contacts. Initial velocity is zero and gravity is standard Earth gravity. For stable manipulation with SDF collision and small features, 120 Hz scene stepping is recommended; 60 Hz is acceptable for slow placement-only scenarios.
